mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% over a quarter signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the quarters when real GDP growth declines by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when industrial production increases by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 over a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when nonfarm payrolls decrease by more than 100,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers by more than 0.5% over a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the CPI increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real GDP and housing starts by more than 1% each over a quarter signals a robust demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth and consumer confidence strengthen.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the quarters when both real GDP and housing starts increase by more than 1%.
